Hands-On Exercise 01

1. Getting Started: Loading R Packages

Using the p_load function of pacman package, I will load sf and tidyverse R packages into the R environment.

pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse)
<!-- ## Importing Data -->

2. Importing Geospatial Data

Using the st_read() of sf package, I will be loading the following three geospatial data and converting them to the desired formats:

  • MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL, a polygon feature layer in GeoJSON format, which will be converted to an ESRI shapefile format;

  • PreSchoolsLocation, point feature layer in GeoJSON format, which will be converted to a KML file format; and

  • CyclingPath, a line feature layer in ESRI shapefile format.

2.1 Importing polygon feature data and coverting to shapefile format (MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL)

Using the st_read() function of sf package, I will be importing the polygon feature layer in GeoJSON format file MP14_SUBZONE_WEB_PL into R. I will also be converting it from a GeoJSON format to an ESRI shapefile format using the st_write() function. To ensure that any existing file is not overwritten, I have included a delete_dsn = FALSE argument and #| eval: false chunk option to display the code in the final rendered code but prevents RStudio from executing it during the rendering process to prevent an error.

mpsz <- st_read("data/geospatial/MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL.geojson")
Reading layer `MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL' from data source 
  `C:\kayc134\ISSS626_kayc\Hands-on_Ex\Hands-on_Ex01\data\geospatial\MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL.geojson' 
  using driver `GeoJSON'
Simple feature collection with 323 features and 13 fields
Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
Dimension:     XY
Bounding box:  xmin: 103.6057 ymin: 1.158699 xmax: 104.0885 ymax: 1.470775
Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
dir.create("data/geospatial/mpsz", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) #create folder

st_write(mpsz, "data/geospatial/mpsz/MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL.shp", 
         driver = "ESRI Shapefile", delete_dsn = FALSE) #write files in ESRI format and prevent overwrite
Reading layer `MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL' from data source 
  `C:\kayc134\ISSS626_kayc\Hands-on_Ex\Hands-on_Ex01\data\geospatial\MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL.geojson' 
  using driver `GeoJSON'
Simple feature collection with 323 features and 13 fields
Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
Dimension:     XY
Bounding box:  xmin: 103.6057 ymin: 1.158699 xmax: 104.0885 ymax: 1.470775
Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84

The message above reveals that the geospatial objects are multipolygon features. There are a total of 323 multipolygon features and 13 fields in mpsz simple feature data frame. mpsz is in WGS 84, which is a geodetic system and thusgeographic (3D/spherical) rather than projected (2D/flat). The bounding box provides the x extend and y extend of the data.

2.2 Importing point feature layer and coverting to KML format (PreSchoolsLocation)

Similary, using the st_read() function of sf package, I will be importing the point feature layer in GeoJSON format file PreSchoolsLocation into R. I will also be converting it from a GeoJSON format to KML format using the st_write() function. To ensure that any existing file is not overwritten, I have included a delete_dsn = FALSE argument and #| eval: false chunk option to display the code in the final rendered code but prevents RStudio from executing it during the rendering process to prevent an error.

preschool <- st_read("data/geospatial/PreSchoolsLocation.geojson")
Reading layer `PreSchoolsLocation' from data source 
  `C:\kayc134\ISSS626_kayc\Hands-on_Ex\Hands-on_Ex01\data\geospatial\PreSchoolsLocation.geojson' 
  using driver `GeoJSON'
Simple feature collection with 2290 features and 2 fields
Geometry type: POINT
Dimension:     XYZ
Bounding box:  xmin: 103.6878 ymin: 1.247759 xmax: 103.9897 ymax: 1.462134
z_range:       zmin: 0 zmax: 0
Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
dir.create("data/geospatial/preschool", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) #create folder

st_write(preschool, "data/geospatial/preschool/preschool.kml", 
         driver = "KML", delete_dsn = FALSE) #write files and prevent overwrite
Reading layer `PreSchoolsLocation' from data source 
  `C:\kayc134\ISSS626_kayc\Hands-on_Ex\Hands-on_Ex01\data\geospatial\PreSchoolsLocation.geojson' 
  using driver `GeoJSON'

The message above reveals that preschool is a point feature data frame. There are a total of 2290 features and 2 fields. preschool is in WGS 84, which is the same as mpsz.

2.3 Importing polyline feature data in shapefile format (CyclingPath)

The code chunk below uses st_read() function of sf package to import CyclingPath shapefile into R as a line feature data frame.

cyclingpath = st_read(dsn = "data/geospatial/CyclingPath", 
                         layer = "CyclingPath")
Reading layer `CyclingPath' from data source

There are a total of 4830 features and 7 fields in cyclingpath sf data frame. The geospatial entities are capture in multilinestring object. Unlike the earlier two data sets, this data set is in SVY21 projected coordinates system.

3. Checking the Content of a Simple Feature Data Frame

Before performing data wrangling, I will be learning more about the mpsz data set using st_geometry(), glimpse() and head().

The glimpse() report reveals the data type of each fields. For example, SUBZONE_NO is in integer data type, SUBZONE_N, CA_IND, PLN_AREA_N and REGION_N fields are in character data type, and SHAPE_1.AREA and SHAPE_1.LEN fields are in double-precision values.

It should be noted that FMEL_UPD_D is showing as a 14-digit character rather than a date type. The 14 digits should be referring to the year, month, date, hour, minute and second in a “YYYYMMDDHHMMSS” format and will need to be converted using ymd_hms() within a mutate() function, which is part of the tidyverse package. I also dropped the time using as_date().

mpsz <- mpsz %>%
  mutate(FMEL_UPD_D = as_date(ymd_hms (FMEL_UPD_D))) #convert to date and drops the time

glimpse(mpsz) #verify that it has been converted to date
